messages.subject: dplyr function conflicts
messages.body_plain: I have lots of code using dplyr syntax to manipulate data. I added some new packages and suddenly there is problem with select, but also with summarize functions. I hate writing dplyr::select, because it makes code unreadable. Is there a way to resolve this conflict? Are there any suggestions made to developers?

messages.subject: Re: dplyr function conflicts
messages.body_plain:
What are you loading that is overridding dplyr::select?

Typically, the preference is to load tidyverse packages last so that they mush everything loaded before, but if you need the functions in another package then that's no good either.

You could try the new conflicted package to "prefer" one over the other.

https://github.com/r-lib/conflicted

HTH,
B

messages.subject: Re: dplyr function conflicts
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the ideas, I really like the conflicted package.
I am using RStudio and I think once I load a package I cannot load it again. So typically, I write some code that works, and then if I need to reexecute, it doesn't. Often, I don't know what is the conflicting package, my guess is mainly MASS, because lots of functions I use depend on other functions in MASS. But for example, summarize also stopped working now, and as far as I know, there is no summarize function in MASS.

To sum up, conflicted package seems to work now, I hope this solves my issues in the long turn.

Have a nice day,

Kristof

messages.body_snippet:
Hello manipulators,

When I run the example code of mutate (https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/mutate.html), it did not make new variable...
Is there something wrong in this code?

> head(mtcars)

messages.subject: Re: Trouble to add variables by mutate
messages.subject_clean: Trouble to add variables by mutate
messages.body_plain:
It did make them. I’ve highlighted them below.

You need to save your new dataset and then you can examine with head()

mtcars2 <-

mtcars %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(

       cyl2 = cyl * 2,

       cyl4 = cyl2 * 2

     )

head(mtcars2)
